nodes.label: Jeremy Bentham
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: British philosopher (1748-1832). Founder of utilitarianism. Greatest happiness of the greatest number. Felicific calculus to measure pleasure and pain. Criticized for ignoring minority rights and reducing justice to aggregate utility.

nodes.label: Natural Rights
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Rights inherent to human beings by nature, not granted by any authority. Life, liberty, and property (Locke). Exist prior to and independent of government. Influenced American and French revolutions. Basis for human rights theory.

nodes.label: Three Generations of Rights
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: First generation: civil and political rights (freedom, equality, voting). Second generation: economic, social, cultural rights (education, health, work). Third generation: collective rights (self-determination, development, clean environment). Progressive evolution.

nodes.label: Negative Rights
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Rights requiring the state to refrain from action: not to censor, not to arrest arbitrarily, not to discriminate. First-generation rights. Most fundamental rights in Indian Constitution are negative rights limiting state power.

nodes.label: Social Contract Theory
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Theory that political authority is based on agreement among individuals to form a society and government. Hobbes: absolute authority to avoid chaos. Locke: limited government protecting natural rights. Rousseau: general will of the people.

nodes.label: Rights and the State
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: The state is both the protector and potential violator of rights. Constitutional rights limit state power. State must not only refrain from violating rights but also protect citizens from rights violations by others. Balancing act between security and liberty.

nodes.label: French Revolution and Democracy
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: The 1789 French Revolution was a landmark in modern democracy, inspiring democratic struggles across Europe. Democracy in France was overthrown and restored several times throughout the 19th century.
